itemListElement.name: Sprint Retrospective Samples for US Scrum Teams in 2026: Template, 5 Formats and 40 Questions

acceptedAnswer.text: A sprint retrospective is a Scrum event at the end of each sprint where the team reviews how it worked and agrees on improvements for the next sprint. People, process, tools and the definition of done are all in scope. It ends with 1 to 3 action items, each with an owner.

mainEntity.name: How long should a sprint retrospective be?

acceptedAnswer.text: At most 3 hours for a 1-month sprint, per the Scrum Guide's timebox, and the guide says shorter sprints usually need less. It sets no floor, so 45 to 90 minutes for a 2-week sprint is convention rather than rule (industry estimate). The 7-part agenda above runs 55 minutes.

mainEntity.name: What are the 3 questions of a sprint retrospective?

acceptedAnswer.text: The classic 3 questions are: What went well? What did not go well? What will we do differently next sprint? Put the answers into your chosen format, then vote on the top 2 issues and agree on 1 to 3 actions, each with an owner and a due date.

mainEntity.name: How often should sprint retrospectives happen?

acceptedAnswer.text: Once per sprint. The Scrum Guide says the retrospective concludes the Sprint, so it sits after the sprint review and before the next planning. Improvements can go straight into the next Sprint Backlog, which is the part most teams skip when they postpone the retro by a week.

The Scrum team, which the Scrum Guide defines as 1 Scrum Master, 1 Product Owner and the developers, with no sub-teams inside it. Stakeholders belong in the sprint review instead. Keeping retros team-only makes people readier to raise problems honestly, so keep the group small and consistent.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a sprint review and a retrospective?

acceptedAnswer.text: The sprint review inspects the product increment with stakeholders, while the retrospective inspects how the team worked and plans improvements. Both happen at the end of each sprint, with the review first.
